correctness.rationale: The exact sum-distance rule classifies 3n maximal tetrahedral facets for n>=7. A nine-phase list of codimension-one free faces collapses 9n pairs to precisely the n-edge rim. Each freeness comparison is confined to six incident facets and earlier translated pairs in integer columns [-3,3], injective modulo n>=7; exact symbolic checks confirm all nine universal identities without substituting any n. For n=3 the complex is a simplex, n=4 cross-polytope boundary; for n=5 and n=6 independently listed 25 and 18 validated elementary pairs reduce to 2-dimensional simply-connected complexes with Euler characteristics 2 and 4, hence S2 and wedge3 S2 by Hurewicz/Whitehead. Original graph surjects on pi1 via distance-two triangle fillings and rung squares, and the rim bounds for n<=6. A standard-library verifier reconstructs all small cases and independently replays 3996 large-n collapse pairs as corroboration, without treating finite n as an all-n proof. Later Rips scales are outside the theorem.

value.rationale: The cyclic prism is a canonical finite two-row graph family singled out by the metric-gluing literature as a natural hard metric-graph topology question. Across the natural integer parameter n, its scale-two Rips topology exhibits a sharp 3-sphere to 2-sphere-wedge to circle transition, with an explicit universal simple-homotopy reduction for every n>=7. The supported integral H1 inclusion-rank statement gives additional persistence-relevant information. This is a complete natural two-parameter-scale slice rather than an arbitrary finite census or an isolated trivial invariant.
